title: Form Validator
description: Build a form validation library that checks email format, required fields, length constraints, and returns error messages.

steps.title: validateEmail function
steps.description: Write `validateEmail(email)` that returns `true` if the email contains both `@` and `.` characters, and `false` otherwise.
hints: Use the includes() method to check for '@' and '.'

codeTemplate.python:
def validate_email(email):
    # Your code here

print(validate_email('test@example.com'))
print(validate_email('invalid'))

verification.failureMessage: Return true for valid emails and false for invalid ones.

steps.title: validateRequired function
steps.description: Write `validateRequired(value)` that returns `true` if the value is not empty, not null, and not undefined. For strings, trim before checking.
hints: Check if value is null or undefined first
For strings, use .trim() to remove whitespace
Return true only if value is non-empty after trimming

codeTemplate.python:
def validate_required(value):
    # Your code here

print(validate_required('hello'))
print(validate_required('   '))
print(validate_required(None))

verification.failureMessage: Return false for empty, null, or whitespace-only values.

steps.title: validateLength function
steps.description: Write `validateLength(value, min, max)` that returns `true` if the value's length is between min and max (inclusive), and `false` otherwise.
hints: Return true only if both conditions are met

codeTemplate.python:
def validate_length(value, min_len, max_len):
    # Your code here

print(validate_length('hello', 3, 10))
print(validate_length('hi', 3, 10))
print(validate_length('hello world!', 3, 10))

verification.failureMessage: Return true only when length is between min and max inclusive.

steps.title: validateForm function
steps.description: Write `validateForm(fields, rules)` where `fields` is an object of field values and `rules` is an object of validation rule arrays. Return `true` if all fields pass their rules.
hints: Each rule is an object with { validate, params }
Iterate over each field and check all its rules
Use .every() or loop with early return

verification.failureMessage: Return true only when all fields pass their validation rules.

steps.title: Errors object with messages
steps.description: Extend `validateForm` to return an `errors` object with field names as keys and arrays of error messages as values, instead of a boolean.
hints: Push descriptive messages like 'Email is invalid' for failed rules
Return the errors object (empty means valid)

verification.failureMessage: Return an object with field keys and arrays of error messages.
